title.rendered: Run With Endurance the Race Marked Out for You: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Throw off the weight. Strip the entanglement. Run the race marked out for you. And keep your eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of your faith.

content.rendered:
Throw off the weight. Strip the entanglement. Run the race marked out for you. And keep your eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of your faith.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, June 11, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles. And let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us, fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith.”
Hebrews 12:1-2 (NIV)

Today’s Message

The writer of Hebrews has just finished walking us through a long hall of faithful saints in chapter eleven. Abel. Enoch. Noah. Abraham. Sarah. Moses. Rahab. Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel. Faithful men and women who endured against every kind of resistance and held the line of faith until they passed it to the next generation. And then chapter twelve opens with one word that changes everything: therefore.

Therefore, since you are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses. The Christian life is a race, and you are not running it on an empty track. You are running it in a stadium filled with believers from every era of church history, every nation, every generation, who finished their leg and are now cheering you on yours. Their faithfulness becomes the encouragement for your endurance.

And the instructions for the race are three. First, throw off the weight. The Greek word means to strip away. A runner does not race in a winter coat. A believer cannot run with the accumulated weight of unconfessed sin, of anxieties not laid down, of comparisons not crucified, of disappointments not surrendered. Strip it. Drop it. Run lighter.

Second, throw off the sin that so easily entangles. Notice the verb. Sin does not just slow you down. It tangles your legs. The sins we have been winking at for years do not stay in the corner. They wrap around the ankles and trip the runner. The writer is not condemning. He is freeing. There is a way to run unentangled.

Third, run with perseverance the race marked out for you. Not someone else’s race. Yours. Marked out for you. By God. With Spirit-empowered endurance.

And the secret of running this way is one direction of gaze. Fixing our eyes on Jesus. The pioneer who has already run the race ahead of you. The perfecter who is making your faith complete. The One who, for the joy set before Him, endured the cross. Keep your eyes there. Not on the runner next to you. Not on the distance left. Not on the pain in your side. On Him. The whole race is run by the one looking at Him.

Prayer

Father, today I throw off every weight that has been slowing me down. I lay down what I have been carrying that was never mine to carry. I confess the sin that has been tangling my feet and step away from it. And I fix my eyes on Jesus, who has already run this race and is bringing me home. By Your Spirit, give me endurance for the lap ahead. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses. I throw off every weight. I strip away the sin that entangles. I run the race marked out for me with perseverance. My eyes are fixed on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of my faith. I will finish.
